purpose: One primary-source lookup per unsized link. Contrasts preserve source units, populations and horizons. No coefficient is admitted to runtime. A numeric contrast may be descriptive or use an incompatible denominator; see evidenceLimit.

rows.range: 7–22 additional quality-of-life arrests; range across IV strategies, not a confidence interval
rows.unit: annual arrest count per additional full-time sworn officer
rows.horizon: Officer employment in previous year predicts arrests in current year; city-year panel 1981–2018, COPS-IV 1990–2018
rows.population: 242 large U.S. cities, population above 50,000 in 1980
rows.evidenceLimit: Two IV strategies; local/historical hiring effects. Not arrests per officer per month or generic rate elasticity. Larger drug/liquor arrest increases per capita for Black civilians.

rows.range: 43% reduction; 3.95 fewer violent-crime arrests per 100 youth; confidence interval unavailable in checked abstract
rows.unit: violent-crime arrests per 100 youth assigned to program versus control
rows.horizon: 16 months after random assignment; eight-week summer program
rows.population: 1,634 disadvantaged Chicago high-school youth
rows.evidenceLimit: Randomized assignment effect, not an effect per additional place-level slot or universal participant compliance.

rows.range: approximately one fewer city resident per additional reported crime; confidence interval unavailable in checked abstract
rows.unit: net city population count per reported crime
rows.horizon: Annual city-level panel; exact behavioral migration lag unavailable
rows.population: U.S. cities; household analysis emphasizes families with children and higher incomes
rows.evidenceLimit: IV supports crime-to-flight direction. Net population decline is not gross out-migration probability; all reported crimes differ from violent crimes per 100,000.

rows.range: 10.8% lower prematurity and 11.8% lower low birth weight; confidence interval unavailable in checked abstract
rows.unit: relative birth-outcome incidence after E-ZPass adoption, within 2 km versus 2–10 km
rows.horizon: Pregnancy exposure followed by birth; exact adoption-to-birth lag unavailable in checked abstract
rows.population: Mothers residing near toll plazas
rows.evidenceLimit: Quasi-experimental adoption contrast, not per congestion-index point. Working-paper prematurity definition (<38 weeks) needs reconciliation with standard <37 weeks.

rows.range: 10-unit decrease in birth-year TSP associated with 1% higher annual earnings; confidence interval unavailable
rows.unit: percent annual earnings per 10-unit reduction in total suspended particulates; concentration unit unavailable in checked landing-page abstract
rows.horizon: Exposure in birth year; annual earnings at ages 29–31
rows.population: U.S. birth cohorts in counties affected differently by 1970 Clean Air Act
rows.evidenceLimit: Primary 2013 working-paper estimate; final 2017 article abstract confirms direction but this version-specific number needs final-table reconciliation. Not PM2.5 or PM10 conversion.

rows.range: 6.1% increase in low-birth-weight probability for any violation; 6.5% for chemical violation; confidence interval unavailable
rows.unit: relative low-birth-weight probability for pregnancy exposure versus no violation exposure
rows.horizon: Violations during gestation, birth outcomes
rows.population: New Jersey births 1997–2007; stronger findings for less-educated mothers
rows.evidenceLimit: Primary full-text indexed passage verified; later page access challenged. Binary gestational exposure differs from violations per water system. Chemical and any-violation estimates are separate contrasts, not a continuous range.

rows.range: 75% decline in mortality impact of days with mean temperature above 80°F; per-hot-day death coefficient unavailable
rows.unit: relative decline in historical temperature-mortality effect
rows.horizon: Twentieth-century comparison; monthly mortality aggregation; exact acute lag unavailable
rows.population: U.S. population in historical state panel
rows.evidenceLimit: Air conditioning explains adaptation in study; 75% is not a universal mortality multiplier. Daily mean >80°F differs from game daily high ≥90°F.

rows.unit: Exact absence-rate coefficient per ppm unavailable in checked primary abstract
rows.horizon: Daily pollution linked to school absence; exact lag unavailable
rows.population: Texas school students
rows.evidenceLimit: Primary abstract verifies high CO increases absences below federal standards. Does not supply a generic linear per-ppm slope.

rows.unit: Exact AC-use change per electricity-price change unavailable in checked source
rows.horizon: Experimental pricing event days; exact persistence unavailable
rows.population: 280 study households; survey responses from 162
rows.evidenceLimit: Primary experiment measures energy conservation/AC use under event pricing. It does not verify reduction in AC ownership share or a universal low-income/elderly slope.

rows.range: 50–100% higher mortality in year after displacement; 10–15% higher annual death hazards after twenty years; reported estimate ranges, not confidence intervals
rows.unit: relative annual death hazard versus expected undisplaced-worker hazard
rows.horizon: First post-displacement year and twenty years later; death records 1980–2006
rows.population: High-seniority male Pennsylvania workers, employment records in 1970s–1980s
rows.evidenceLimit: Administrative mass-displacement analysis; does not establish three-year exponential half-life or effects for every worker.

rows.range: 35% higher stroke risk; 17% higher ischemic-heart-disease death risk; confidence intervals unavailable in checked announcement
rows.unit: relative risk for ≥55 versus 35–40 working hours per week
rows.horizon: Long-term exposure; exact common duration unavailable in checked WHO announcement
rows.population: Workers in global WHO/ILO synthesis
rows.evidenceLimit: Stroke endpoint is stroke risk, not specifically stroke mortality. Pooled observational evidence does not supply an incremental effect per exposure year.

rows.unit: Exact metabolic-syndrome coefficient or per-childhood-year dose unavailable in checked primary abstract
rows.horizon: Childhood access, adult health; exact measured ages unavailable in checked abstract
rows.population: U.S. cohorts exposed to historical Food Stamp rollout
rows.evidenceLimit: Primary article verifies lower adult metabolic syndrome. County program availability is not identical to individual receipt years.

rows.range: SPM child poverty 5.2% in 2021 and 12.4% in 2022; descriptive levels, not treatment-effect range
rows.unit: percent of children below Supplemental Poverty Measure threshold
rows.horizon: Annual calendar-year income/resources: 2021 versus 2022
rows.population: U.S. children in Census poverty statistics
rows.evidenceLimit: CTC/EITC temporary expansions and stimulus ended together. This before/after comparison does not identify a causal slope per benefit dollar; Census notes subsequent SPM revisions.

rows.unit: Parent-incarceration household-income coefficient unavailable
rows.horizon: Defendant employment follow-up; household-income horizon unavailable
rows.population: Pretrial criminal defendants, not specifically incarcerated parents and their children
rows.evidenceLimit: Cited Dobbie/Goldin/Yang source identifies pretrial detention effects on defendants formal employment and benefits using judge assignment. It does not verify this household-parent linkage.

rows.range: 0.31 additional completed education years; about 7% higher wages and 3.2 percentage-point lower annual adult poverty as separate outcomes; confidence interval unavailable
rows.unit: completed education years per 10% increase in per-pupil spending in every one of 12 school years
rows.horizon: Sustained 12-year public-school exposure; adult attainment
rows.population: U.S. school-finance-reform cohorts; effects larger for low-income children
rows.evidenceLimit: Event-study/IV reform estimate; published 2016 estimate differs from updated working-paper abstract (0.27). Not one-month budget change.

rows.unit: Exact graduation coefficient per eligibility year unavailable in checked primary abstract
rows.horizon: Childhood expansions in 1980s–1990s, later educational completion; exact age unavailable
rows.population: Low-income U.S. children
rows.evidenceLimit: Primary abstract verifies higher high-school/college completion; widely quoted 10%/6% figures not verified in the checked primary source. Eligibility differs from actual coverage.

rows.range: 1.3% higher earnings; confidence interval unavailable
rows.unit: percent earnings per 1 SD improvement in teacher value-added in one grade
rows.horizon: One grade of exposure; earnings at age 28
rows.population: Students linked to teacher and adult tax records
rows.evidenceLimit: Quasi-experimental teacher value-added study; not cumulative per-year multiplier or all teacher-quality measures.

rows.range: about 4 percentile points in first small-class year; about 1 additional percentile point per subsequent year; confidence interval unavailable
rows.unit: standardized-test percentile points, small 13–17 versus regular 22–25 students
rows.horizon: First year and subsequent school years during four-year STAR experiment
rows.population: 11,600 Tennessee kindergarten-entry students and teachers beginning 1985–1986
rows.evidenceLimit: Randomized classroom contrast; percentile points differ from SDs. Do not linearly convert the categorical treatment to each one-pupil reduction.

rows.range: 6.0 percentage-point increase in high-school graduation; 8.3 points higher on-time college enrollment as separate outcome; confidence interval unavailable
rows.unit: absolute completion/enrollment probability points for preschool attendance
rows.horizon: Age-four preschool exposure followed to high-school completion and approximately 20 years after enrollment
rows.population: More than 4,000 randomized Boston four-year-old applicants, admissions cohorts 1997–2003
rows.evidenceLimit: Lottery-offer IV estimates attendance effect for compliers. Source verifies Boston result; Tennessee sixth-grade results mentioned but no independently verified coefficient. Not general quality-score slope.

rows.range: 0.06 SD increase in combined math/reading scores per $1,000 income increase; confidence interval unavailable
rows.unit: child combined test-score standard deviations per $1,000 family income; dollar price year unavailable in checked abstract
rows.horizon: Short run; exact months/years unavailable in checked abstract
rows.population: U.S. children affected by EITC changes; stronger for disadvantaged children
rows.evidenceLimit: EITC-based IV estimate; no monthly conversion and no inflation adjustment fabricated.

rows.range: $3,477 (31%) higher annual income relative to $11,270 control mean; confidence interval unavailable
rows.unit: annual income dollars and percent for families taking up experimental voucher before child age 13
rows.horizon: Moved before age 13; earnings measured in mid-twenties
rows.population: Children from high-poverty housing projects in Moving to Opportunity experiment
rows.evidenceLimit: Randomized voucher/treatment-on-treated effect. This lookup verifies MTO contrast, not the separate Chetty/Hendren 2018 approximately 4%-of-gap-per-year coefficient.

rows.range: Approximately -0.50 SD vocabulary and -0.66 SD reading; across-outcome range, not confidence interval
rows.unit: Standard deviations of assessed child performance after homicide in residential block group
rows.horizon: Homicide less than one week before assessment; effects fade as assessment window widens; exact half-life unavailable
rows.population: African-American children in Chicago community study
rows.evidenceLimit: Timing comparison supports acute effect; no universal child effect or exact seven-day half-life.

rows.range: Unavailable; primary abstract verifies lower high-school completion but does not report exact magnitude
rows.unit: Completion probability among students exposed to nearby police killing; denominator details unavailable
rows.horizon: Persistent schooling effects; exact graduation follow-up unavailable
rows.population: Inner-city students; exact race-specific population unavailable in primary snippet
rows.evidenceLimit: Hyperlocal distance variation; stored 3.5% cannot be treated as percentage points or independently verified here.

rows.range: Unavailable in primary abstract
rows.unit: Mathematics achievement associated with switching schools; exact standardized denominator unavailable
rows.horizon: Unavailable in primary abstract
rows.population: Students switching schools and classmates
rows.evidenceLimit: Disruption and school-quality changes differ; stored -0.03 SD not verified by this lookup.

rows.range: 40% reduction in citizen-noncitizen graduation gap; no graduation-rate effect range available
rows.unit: Percent of preexisting citizen-noncitizen graduation gap, not graduation probability
rows.horizon: Post-DACA; exact measured follow-up unavailable
rows.population: Undocumented youth eligible for temporary work authorization and deportation deferral
rows.evidenceLimit: Gap reduction cannot be converted into percentage-point graduation effect without baseline gap; stored +15% not verified.

rows.range: Unavailable in primary abstract
rows.unit: Return to years of schooling, not separately diploma completion; exact earnings denominator unavailable
rows.horizon: Unavailable
rows.population: People whose compulsory schooling is affected by attendance laws
rows.evidenceLimit: Instrumental-variable schooling return is not a universal graduation earnings premium; no coefficient conversion.

rows.range: -0.76 percentage points for white men; -3.4 percentage points for Black men; group estimates, not confidence interval
rows.unit: Absolute probability difference in incarceration for high-school completion
rows.horizon: Exact age/follow-up horizon unavailable in primary abstract
rows.population: Male cohorts; separately reported white and Black groups
rows.evidenceLimit: Compulsory-schooling identification and descriptive estimates coexist in paper; abstract does not establish these quoted group numbers as the IV estimates. Not an arrest-rate coefficient.

rows.range: Unavailable in primary lookup
rows.unit: Mortality probability per additional school year; exact denominator unavailable
rows.horizon: Unavailable in primary lookup
rows.population: U.S. adults
rows.evidenceLimit: One lookup does not verify disputed original coefficient or later robustness checks; no settled causal range established.

rows.range: -5% to -7% nearby rents
rows.unit: Relative percent difference in nearby rents after a large market-rate apartment building, compared with farther/later-built locations
rows.horizon: After construction; exact duration unavailable
rows.population: Nearby rental units in low-income areas; buildings with 50 or more units; approximately two-block radius
rows.evidenceLimit: Author-institute summary of local quasi-experimental study; no whole-place per-capita construction slope or universal 12-month lag.

rows.range: Effect slope unavailable; source describes acceleration above 32% rent burden
rows.unit: Rent burden as percent local median income; homelessness rate denominator unavailable
rows.horizon: 2017 homeless counts and 2018 Q3 affordability cited; causal lag unavailable
rows.population: 386 of 399 U.S. Continuums of Care, covering 98.7% of counted homeless population in 2017
rows.evidenceLimit: Descriptive modeled association; 32% is an inflection description, not a causal discontinuity or measured slope; 22% not independently verified.

rows.range: +3.4 percentage points IV; +3.1 percentage points OLS; estimator comparison, not confidence interval
rows.unit: Absolute probability difference in emergency shelter use per tenant eviction order; nonevicted mean 0.9%
rows.horizon: Year after eviction case filing; second-year effect unavailable in this lookup
rows.population: Filed-case tenants in Chicago/New York study; marginal tenants for judge-stringency IV
rows.evidenceLimit: Shelter use is not all homelessness. IV pertains to marginal eviction-order cases; not per county eviction-rate point.

rows.range: +0.188 visits quarters 1–4; -0.113 visits quarters 5–8; separate horizon estimates, not confidence interval
rows.unit: Additional hospital-visit count per tenant after eviction order
rows.horizon: Quarters 1–4 and 5–8 after case filing, separately
rows.population: New York tenants with hospital records in eviction-case study
rows.evidenceLimit: Judge-stringency IV local effect. Second-period estimate uncertain; negative estimate does not prove reversal. No annualized or whole-place rate conversion.

rows.range: Unavailable in primary abstract; increased unemployment verified qualitatively
rows.unit: Neighborhood unemployment rate following transit access loss; exact denominator unavailable
rows.horizon: Hurricane Sandy October 29, 2012 and subsequent service loss; exact follow-up unavailable
rows.population: Affected New York City neighborhoods, especially transit-dependent subgroups
rows.evidenceLimit: Natural experiment; secondary summary reports 1.4 pp but primary lookup did not verify coefficient; no per-resident transit-service slope.

rows.range: Approximately +1.8 percentage points; confidence interval unavailable
rows.unit: County employment-rate difference when gaining broadband access; exact population denominator unavailable
rows.horizon: U.S. expansion 1999–2007; precise post-access lag unavailable
rows.population: U.S. counties; larger associations in rural and isolated areas
rows.evidenceLimit: County/time fixed-effects association; binary county broadband availability is not household-access share.

rows.range: 17% lower operating cost at IRI 50 than IRI 170
rows.unit: Relative modeled vehicle operating costs per vehicle-mile traveled; IRI inches/mile; small automobile at 50 mph on level straight road
rows.horizon: Per mile of travel; no monthly lag estimated
rows.population: Illustrative small automobile in FHWA HERS model
rows.evidenceLimit: Engineering model example, not household annual-cost causal estimate or slope on game condition index; route, vehicle and speed matter.

rows.range: Roughly +1,500 industry jobs; confidence interval unavailable
rows.unit: Employment count within deal 3-digit industry in winning location versus runner-up
rows.horizon: Post-deal; exact duration unavailable
rows.population: Locations bidding for large firm-specific incentive deals
rows.evidenceLimit: Distinguish estimated industry gain from 1,500 promised jobs in abstract of published JEP article. No strong evidence of broader local/state growth; not jobs per incentive dollar.

rows.range: Unavailable in primary abstract
rows.unit: Birth response to Quebec pronatalist schedule paying up to C$8,000 per child; coefficient denominator unavailable
rows.horizon: Policy introduction; exact conception/birth lag unavailable
rows.population: Quebec families having children
rows.evidenceLimit: Schedule-specific quasi-experiment; stored C$1,000 coefficient, 5–10% and third-child 25% not independently verified; no linear dollar extrapolation.

rows.range: Unavailable in primary abstract; increased marriage take-up verified qualitatively
rows.unit: Marriage take-up among people in same-sex households
rows.horizon: Across legalization rollout; exact response lag unavailable
rows.population: Men and women in same-sex households in BRFSS
rows.evidenceLimit: State/time policy variation; no numerical take-up range verified and not a current cross-place law difference.

rows.range: +5 to +11 basis points; specification range, not confidence interval
rows.unit: Municipal bond borrowing yields following local daily-newspaper closure
rows.horizon: Long-run after closure; exact follow-up unavailable in primary snippet; sample 1996–2015
rows.population: U.S. municipal bonds/counties served by daily newspapers; 1,596 newspapers across 1,266 counties during sample
rows.evidenceLimit: Quasi-experimental identification checks; municipal bond results cannot directly size state general-obligation spread; not universal 12-month lag.

rows.range: Unavailable in author primary lookup
rows.unit: Survey media-trust response to elite criticism; exact scale/denominator unavailable
rows.horizon: Survey experiment; exact delay unavailable
rows.population: Survey respondents; supporter subgroup size unavailable
rows.evidenceLimit: Author lists experiment replication material, but lookup supplies no effect coefficient or durable three-month effect.

rows.range: Approximately +0.5 percentage points vote share per doubling relief payments; confidence interval unavailable
rows.unit: Incumbent presidential party vote share, relative to doubling relief spending before election
rows.horizon: Election following relief spending; data 1988–2004; exact preelection window unavailable
rows.population: Voters in disaster-affected U.S. areas studied
rows.evidenceLimit: Author university summary; observational election/spending relationship with controls, not votes per dollar or guaranteed incumbent response.

rows.range: about $15 future damage mitigated per $1 preparedness; confidence interval unavailable
rows.unit: damage dollars avoided per preparedness dollar
rows.horizon: Future disaster damage; exact years/lag unavailable in checked primary abstract
rows.population: U.S. natural-disaster spending and election-return panel
rows.evidenceLimit: Observational econometric estimate; preparedness differs from relief and effect depends on actual hazard/assets. Not immediate monthly guaranteed saving.

rows.unit: Real-income-growth to incumbent-approval coefficient unavailable in checked primary abstract
rows.horizon: Quarterly observations 1960–2022; exact lag unavailable
rows.population: U.S. presidential approval and macroeconomic series
rows.evidenceLimit: Primary study emphasizes gasoline prices/inflation expectations after controls; no verified causal real-income-growth slope or place-level approval adapter.

rows.range: 110 months average prison sentence for offenses carrying mandatory minimum versus 28 months without; descriptive comparison
rows.unit: months sentenced per federal convicted offender
rows.horizon: Fiscal year 2016 sentencing; no causal 12-month prison-stock response verified
rows.population: Federal offenders sentenced in FY2016
rows.evidenceLimit: Different offense/severity composition and 38.7% received relief. Descriptive sentence comparison is not mandatory-minimum causal effect on incarcerated per 100,000.

rows.range: 11% lower indebtedness; 24% fewer other delinquent accounts; confidence interval unavailable
rows.unit: relative borrower total debt and count of other delinquent accounts
rows.horizon: Post-discharge outcomes; income follow-up three years, exact delinquency horizon unavailable in checked abstract
rows.population: Defaulted private student-loan borrowers affected by National Collegiate chain-of-title discharge episode
rows.evidenceLimit: Plausibly random legal discharge; source versions differ (earlier revision: 26% debt reduction and 11% lower other-account default). Keep this NBER landing-page version separate; not universal forgiveness or dollar past-due balance.

rows.range: 5.2 million more labor-force participants projected in 2033 than prior forecast, mostly from higher net immigration
rows.unit: national civilian labor-force persons, forecast revision relative to prior baseline
rows.horizon: 2024–2034 projection window; comparison at 2033
rows.population: U.S. civilian noninstitutionalized population aged 16+
rows.evidenceLimit: CBO projection revision, not isolated causal immigrant-admission coefficient or general law-in-force multiplier; admissions scale, age, participation, and policy matter.

rows.range: Unavailable; schooling effects mostly statistically insignificant
rows.unit: Child schooling outcomes after randomized voucher lottery; exact graduation coefficient/denominator unavailable
rows.horizon: Children tracked 14 years after 1997 Chicago lottery
rows.population: Children of Chicago applicants; 82,607 lottery applicants
rows.evidenceLimit: Randomized offer estimates; abstract does not provide graduation estimate/CI. Insignificance is not measured zero or universal voucher-entitlement effect.

rows.range: Unavailable; exact arrest effect range unavailable
rows.unit: Child criminal involvement/arrest outcomes after randomized housing voucher lottery
rows.horizon: Long-term after 1997 Chicago lottery; exact arrest window unavailable in primary abstract
rows.population: Children in Chicago voucher-applicant families
rows.evidenceLimit: Lottery identification does not translate to statewide crime index; no verified zero or coefficient from abstract.

rows.range: Ban effect unavailable; exact return spread unavailable in lookup
rows.unit: Stock trading returns of members of Congress and immediate families, not effect of prohibition
rows.horizon: Stock activity 2012–2023; investment holding-return horizon unavailable
rows.population: All U.S. members of Congress and immediate families in source dataset
rows.evidenceLimit: Descriptive trading performance is not an implemented-ban counterfactual or evidence a ban has zero effect.

rows.range: Reading-score effect unavailable; 4,240 unique titles targeted in 2023 is descriptive exposure context
rows.unit: Unique titles challenged, not removals or reading-proficiency percentage points
rows.horizon: Calendar year 2023 for challenges; reading-response lag unavailable
rows.population: U.S. library/school censorship reports gathered by ALA
rows.evidenceLimit: Challenge count neither proves removal nor estimates reading score effects; no causal law-to-reading coefficient.
